I do not recommend it right now, and I have yet to finish it. I recommend waiting until the future to buy it, but let me list the pros so I don't just seem like I'm complaining.
1. It's very beautiful on max settings, a revolutionary experience looking at these animatronics and environments in beautiful computer-busting ultra graphics. 
2. There are horror segments in this game that are stellar, I love them.
3. Mapping out a route ahead of time, using Freddy as a desperate last attempt to escape imminent doom just hits the right way, and the sprinting feels fast while having a reasonable amount of stamina.

Now the cons I have are mainly just the fact that this game is an early birth and should've been put back in the oven before the hamster behind Steel Wool fell asleep on the release button.
1. Optimization is just... garbage. My set up isn't top tier NASA computer, but it can reliably play taxing games at high frame rates, but this game just obliterates the set up. The rendering is sometimes just egregious and I have gotten stuck in an unloaded chunk way more often than I should for a $40 game.
2. Bugs. Bugs galore. Bugs everywhere. 
3. The animatronics, I can run around a corner with a dead end and they'll actually lose me. I genuinely hope this is just a bug and not how this is meant to be published, because this ruins the anxiety of being chased when I know that safety is a turn away. I only have my word as proof but I swear I lost an animatronic just running around a food stand, this is incredibly stupid.
4. Teleporting animatronics, because that's what the game needed. I would love to say that this is a bug, but it doesn't seem so. Apparently, the patrol S.T.A.F.F have mastered magic, because they can teleport to the beginning of their routes and they can also just teleport animatronics over to you. 
5. Texture pop in so blatant it makes games from 2015 look more advanced. I started off playing on low settings, and there are times where I couldn't read signs because I had to wait for the textures to load. 

Just... just please wait for the game to be fixed. Buying it now would only reaffirm that Steel Wool can get away with releasing unfinished product.

edit: There are people saying "It's the fans fault for yelling at Scott Cawthon/Steel Wool to release it early." I don't believe that people wanting to play a game sooner should impact the quality of the game, since you should still release the game at a finished, not as buggy release. There are great games that have had a lot of hype before release and still come out at a good standard. And as of this edit, all the issues in this review are still there, even when I've upgraded my hardware over the holidays. I do love this game, but the flaws of it's current status shouldn't be ignored or glossed over, when the issues have been resolved, this will become a positive review.

edit2: This game has had no serious update that fixes any of the complaints listed in this review, it's been around a month and the closest thing we've seen is fixes for minor things. As I've played more, not only have my complaints remained, but more have accumulated. This game shouldn't have been released like this. At this rate, I'm so close to saying don't ever buy this game, save the money and go buy a sandwich or something.

[b] Updated [/b]

[b] 1) [/b] There is no sense of direction as the game is trying to be both linear and open world. There are no map icons or repeated hints from the characters to somehow direct the player. Doors and specific locations lack the fundamentals of game design and seem to hide themselves from the player instead of being rightfully obvious. More likely than not you will get lost several times while playing this when the solution to progress should be painfully obvious.

[b] 2) [/b] The AI is terribly designed and more of a chore to work around. Animatronics will teleport instead of naturally having to hunt and look for you, they almost always know where you are. Whether or not you are hidden/safe is unclear and the hiding/distraction mechanics rarely come into play and can actually get you killed. Security bots are just thrown into environments as some pathetic means of creating tension and stealth when it's just an exercise in futility once an actual bot spawns. The animatronics are really just annoying obstacles at times and will get in the way rather than pose as a threat, leaving players often stuck or no choice but to game over.

[b] 3) [/b] The saving system is a joke. Why are we still doing this savepoint garbage in anything? You will almost guarantee to see a YouTuber run into this issue if you're planning on watching a playthrough, as the spaces between save points are ridiculous and will send players back miles in progress from guaranteed, unfair deaths. I have repeated multiple segments after being unable to find the savepoint or otherwise being spontaneously game-overed out of nowhere.

[b] 4) [/b] Give the player something to do for once. I am baffled that we are in a game expanding an entire mall but exploration is rewarded with nothing but bad texturing and bloated gigs of empty rooms. Like most, I figured a mall would let us mess around and do fun little games from time to time, especially with the concept art and general idea of the location itself. But no, other than finding collectibles for an achievement there is zero reason to peek around every corner, which is pitiful coming from a Five Nights at Freddy's product.

[b] 5) [/b] This game's optimization should be an obvious problem for anyone with eyes. Even with high graphics settings you'd be too wishful to think most of the textures will render in properly. What is even weirder is that not all the textures appear to be affected by your graphics settings and are either stuck looking clear or completely dead. The camera system in-game is this gaudy, seizure-inducing mess of visual clutter. An issue like this has been a staple for near every FNAF game and I cannot fathom why no one working on these things realizes how painful it is to look it.

[b] 6) [/b] After looking through my own playthrough and what others have found this game has shockingly nothing lore-wise. Nothing that was built up in the previous titles is considered and the game rushes forward with no consideration for actual player intrigue. Stuff happens while other things just don't, with most of the teased content just not being in the final product. After a few hours you really start to notice just how much the game does not give you and this is especially shocking for a Five Nights at Freddy's installment.

[b] 7) [/b] Half of the puzzles in this game are rage inducing and can literally leave the player with no choice but to quit. I’m dead serious. God speed to the people who found out the solution to the Mazercise puzzle, otherwise I would have just had to end my run permanently. I thoroughly refuse to buy any indication this game was play tested with half the puzzles and missions they let in.

[b] 8) [/b] This one feels inexcusable to me in every possible way but the later end of the game, which is around 3 hours of content, does not have saving enabled at all. The game gives you a choice to leave or stay in the mall to explore the rest of what is going on and if you want an actual normal experience you'd stay. But after that, there's literally zero saving. None. How tf are you going to encourage exploration of more areas, extra missions, and a finale segment but then REMOVE all possibilities to save? If a player gets bugged or just cannot continue playing because of their personal lives, they pretty much have to start over. You can only finish the game if you're ready for a 3-hour play session that you perform flawlessly.

Some of the worst game design choices I've EVER seen in my entire life.

[b] Some final short gripes: [/b]

- Enemies repeat the same five lines of dialogue while you're being hunted
- There's no clear understanding of stealth, robots are often able to see you when you're completely cut from their cone of vision, and it's not clear if the dark protects you in any way
- A stamina meter in an exploration game of this size is the dumbest game design choice I have ever seen in my entire life
- Utilize the hiding and distraction mechanics, they're much too rare and some areas leave player's completely defenseless

Security Breach is considered the worst FNaF game. But it's not, it's just bad AT being a FNaF game.

It's a good, even great game on its own. The price might seem a bit steep (at least to me), but with the free DLC, you're essentially buying two games at once.


Now let's go over the good, the bad and the misunderstood.


1. WHAT SECURITY BREACH DOES RIGHT:

- fun character designs and animations

- the main 4 animatronics (plus Sun) actually have personalities and dialogue (or monologue, more commonly)

- the enemies change over the course of the game based on your actions (to keep it spoiler free), they get progressively more dirty and their attacks, weaknesses and aggression evolve to reflect their... state

- the world design is pretty and very much fits the theme of the game

- pure 3D open-world sandbox with a few branching paths (though you can revisit them later in the game)

- dozens of collectibles to find, along with lore* (we'll get to that)

- a couple of sections that require an actual strategy to pass instead of running around like a headless chicken

- well-hidden easter eggs

- multiple endings*

- poking fun at large corporations

- Freddy being a friend for once <3


2. WHAT SECURITY BREACH DOES WRONG:

- it doesn't really have a story, not one that makes sense, at least

- for FNaF fans: there is a severe lack of lore, and what could be considered lore, doesn't make sense in context with the other games, so it's better not to try to connect it

- the endings don't really explain anything

- sometimes it overexplains things, sometimes it explains nothing at all (when you get to Mazercise, for your own good, look up a guide; the game doesn't give you anything useful)

- the enemies sometimes teleport behind you (especially Chica), which I'd love to put as a bug but it's unfortunately intentional game design

- no difficulty slider (which might be unexpected if this is your first FNaF game)

- Mazercise (cool concept, terrible execution)

- Freddy is very underutilized; even in places he's allowed to go, you can only use him for a couple of minutes at a time before his "state-of-the-art" battery depletes

- camera placement (you spend more time figuring out the angle than looking at them, but you can see yourself and Freddy, so that's neat!)

- save points could be positioned MUCH better, so just save at every opportunity in case there's a long stretch without them ahead


3. SECURITY BREACH'S REPUTATION vs ACTUAL SECURITY BREACH:

- Contrary to popular belief, this game is SCARY at times (*cough* Endos *cough*). The problem is that those sections are few and far between, and the tone shift between "happily exploring the Pizzaplex" and "running for your life from an angry bot constantly charging at you in near-complete darkness" is jarring. Ruin is very different though.

- The game is known for its bugs and for not fixing them over time, but... it's really not that bad. Over the course of my first 16-hour playthrough, apart from visual glitches, I experienced the following (and nothing else) while playing as intended:

1. lag when entering a new area (which is basically a substitute for a loading screen)
2. exactly 1 fatal freeze (had to end quit out of the game through Task Manager) while in Daycare, but no crashes
3. Chica standing in front of my hiding spot despite not seeing me and never moving on (twice)
4. Freddy taking the long route when you call him
5? Roxanne finding me every time when hiding, no matter if she saw me hide or not, but I have a feeling that's intentional because she does a sniffing animation beforehand

I've played games that aren't considered "bug terrariums", which had save corruption, missing textures, performance issues... and my copy of SB has had none of that.
Security Breach, in its current form, is no longer a broken game... unless you try hard enough.

- "It's FNaF for kids." Not really? You play as a kid and the world is vibrant and colorful, but some parts of the game are pretty dark, like (spoilers in this paragraph!) Gregory scrapping Chica in cold blood, taking away her ability to speak and lying to Freddy about it. Or what happens to Vanny and Cassie (Ruin) in some of the endings. Sure, it's not on par with the previous games, but the kid is supposed to be like 10 and he's a complete menace with no remorse.


4. SOME TIPS for you if you've made it this far!

- Open boxes even if you're not after collectibles. The upgrades really help.

- If you ARE after collectibles and easter eggs, you might find it fun to play around with the camera flash in different areas. Not saying anything else ;)

- Never hide while actively being detected (red icon) by the animatronics. Unless you're out of stamina, running has better chances of survival. It also seems that the animatronics each have a different chance of finding you, it goes Roxy > Chica > Monty. Endos and Staff Bots can't find you at all.

- When it comes to Endoskeletons, sprint and look back at the end of every hallway. Don't bother hiding or walking backwards until you're at the very end of the section (start walking backwards as soon as you get the item). You'll get caught a few times, but it's not as nerve-wracking as waiting for them to pass your hiding spot. When you're past *that* section, you should be able to call Freddy to extract you when encountering them again.

- There's an excellent guide (not mine) called "How to beat the Mazercise Puzzle" right here on Steam. As a general tip, use the cameras on your watch rather than the image that is supposedly there to help you with the puzzle.

- You might reach a section, after making pizza for Chica, where the door marked as exit doesn't open. The game doesn't tell you this, but you need to hide behind some forklifts, and she'll open it for you. Maybe it's just me, but this took me SO LONG to figure out. (Roxy also has to open a door for you later in the game, but that's a little trickier to get.)

- Anything to do with generators is a "follow the cable and hope not to get lost" quest.

- (Not my experience, I've never had a single issue in that department, but) If you're having performance issues, turn off ray tracing.

- And most importantly: have fun. Explore. There really isn't much in terms of story, but Security Breach's strongest point is that it manages to stick a lot of fun areas to investigate between the dark, creepy parts.


If this review helped you in any way, and you decide to buy it, I'd be glad if you came back and told me which area is your favorite! Mine is Monty's Gator Golf; they made that 150% more detailed than necessary. Thanks for reading; I applaud your patience :)

People need to be honest about these kinds of games especially when they cost this much money. People are giving this game really great reviews and completely ignoring all of the HYPER GLARING FLAWS that the game has. Some of the game mechanics are so absolutely frustrating that you're going to stop playing or throw something. Check the forums if you don't believe me on what's going on in the game. The forums speak to the issues at a much better level than I can in this review but I'll get into it.

Security Breach is a BEAUTIFUL and well laid out game. The environments are honestly top notch and you really get a sense of wonder as you walk through the halls and the different exhibits that the game has to offer. The voice overs are really well done and the characters feel real enough. It feels like an amusement park that could really exist. They clearly put a lot of thought into the environments and locations that you are going to visit. This part of the game is top notch and it's refreshing to play a horror game that puts so much time into custom assets and designs. 

The story pacing is great as well. The atmosphere and setting that they have created is great. You never feel very safe and are forced to keep moving most of the time and as though you can't sit still in any one area too long. This is helped by the CONSTANTLY patrolling enemies in EVERY SINGLE CORNER OF THE GAME. I am really not exaggerating here. Every area of the game you will be hunted and chased by these animatronic killers and patrol bots. There is almost never a room in the entire game so far that you can just take everything in because you will be caught. Is it a good thing? I don't think so. The game starts to fall apart for me here because you never get to come down from the fear of the bots. Well made horror games will give you a chase and then a period of time where nothing really happens so that you can let your guard down and the next chase is that much more impactful. Not so here. You will be chased and killed in every section of the game. Because they do this, you stop being afraid of robots about 30 minutes into the game. Every section is "Oh right, the wolf is back. Oh and the alligator... and the bird. Okay so they are just here all the time great." It just stops being tension building and leads to you being so oversaturated with them that they are just an annoying obstacle instead of something that should be scary. I will say that the one exception to this is the Moon. The moon can go straight to heck but that's because the day care section is one of the least well thought out designs ever. Let's get into the mechanics. 

What really REALLY brings this game down is the constantly frustrating game mechanics and mission designs. First off you have the absolutely laughable AI that runs the bots. Put a chair or a single flower vase in between you and the robots? You may as well not exist. Many times you can just stand in front of them in the open and they won't see you. It's really a joke. There is a section of the game where you need to balance power on two doors to keep out the enemies and after dying to this section 4 or 5 times (even after beating it but being unable to save, which is another problem entirely) I just sat in between two desk chairs and the AI couldn't see me even though they were looking right at me. Enemies will routinely teleport right to you when you are trying to get through different areas and you should expect to die OFTEN. Let me say that again. YOU ARE GOING TO DIE A GREAT DEAL. It wouldn't be quite such a chore but many sections of the game DO NOT LET YOU SAVE after completing a very challenging area so you are forced to do tedious sections of the game again and again. Again. And Again. And again. For some god awful reasons the developers have chosen to not use auto saves after challenging sections instead opting for a save system similar to Alien Isolation where saving is infrequent and takes 2 - 3 seconds for the save to go through. The difference is that Alien Isolation AI wasn't janky and the game balanced challenge with the ability to take a breath and save your game. 

let's talk about a particularly poor designed section of the game. The day care. You have to start up 5 generators in a playground maze. The issues are numerous. First off the generators are absolutely invisible when the lights go out and you start the mission so finding them is an almost non-option. If you read the forums they pretty much all suggest the same thing. You have to basically MEMORIZE the location of the gens when the lights are on and plan your route through the entire area in order to do it when the lights go out. This is not good game design! You shouldn't have to basically memorize an entire layout of a section of game because it's impossible to do when the lights go out. Not to mention the AI in this room will just RANDOMLY teleport behind / near you so it's impossible to figure out where he is or where you will be safe. I've seen him do it numerous times and it's trash. Having to memorize your route removes all the fear of the entire section because you either do the gens or you die. The section where you have to manage your battery power on the doors later on made me so frustrated that I threw my headset onto my desk and had to stop playing for a bit. The AI will routinely bug out at your doors and not move or follow their routes so you will automatically fail when the battery power goes out. 

Let's talk about saves and your mission objectives. First off when you get a new mission it's usually fairly unclear where that objective needs to be done or what you may need to do there. Objects that you need to collect as mandatory for the game progression are the same design as optional collectibles and upgrades so you can't tell what is important and what is not, so I hope you enjoy scouring everywhere for all of the easter eggs because you may not know what is important and what is not. Saves are infrequently placed and you are going to often get through a tough section or a chase (which is basically the whole game) and you'll die and have to do the entire thing again. Get used to doing things QUITE a few times. Again, if you don't believe me go check the forums on how people feel about the save system. 

That's not even getting into why this game runs like shit often times and constantly drops frames and lags. I have a 5900x, 3080 and 32 gigs of ram and this game STILL cannot run nicely. If you have less specs than this, well good luck. 

I think it's great that fans of the FNAF series are getting another game but holy christ this game is full of bugs and was not ready for a release. That's not even going into the number of people's games who are soft locking and hard locking and causing them to have to start all over. Seriously, this game is a frustrating mess. If you really love the franchise I am sure you will find a way to get through it but my strong suggestion is that you wait for them to make a patch that fixes the majority of these issues. 

tl;dr - Game is a buggy mess and I strongly recommend you view the forums to get a good idea of what you are going to deal with while playing this game. Fanboys are just reviewing the game positively here and not discussing the huge number of issues.

I've played this game 3 years after the release and it's STILL AN UNFINISHED, BUGGY mess.

The Good:
- The Pizzaplex looks amazing, it just makes you want to roam its hallways all day long.
- The animatronic designs are pretty cool.
- Sun and Moon are awesome.
- Monty's area is peak perfect design.

The Bad:
- There are several gamebreaking bugs. If I didn't create a different save file every time, i would have had to restart the game 5 times, because it softlocked. I fell through the map just by walking around, getting out of a hiding place threw me into the void, a door remained locked when I had to go through, animatronics got stuck in walls and on furniture. Even the final bossfight is buggy. It's just ridiculous.
- The map is terrible. The whole Pizzaplex is huge and you literally have no idea where you need to go. At the beginning, it is said that the mission will be marked on your map, but there are no marks on the map, ever. Good luck finding your mission's place somewhere in this huge damn plaza.
- Horrible gameplay mechanics. Sometimes it's random if the roaming roomba security bots notice you or not. The animatronics teleport all over the map, making it unfair. Was Chica behind you when you left a room? Now she is in front of you somehow, too bad, deal with it. 
- Sneaking is useless, why does the one "blind" animatronic "hear" you, when you are sneaking?
- Some puzzles are horrible. F-ck Mazercise and the DJ MM area in particular. 
- Vanny. Vanny, the "big bad" of this game, shows up a total of 1 time. Not like she does anything that time, she just hops around like the lunatic she is. What a great villain. I'm pretty sure they scrapped her scenes for some reason.
- William, this hot garbage of a man, also appears, but not even he knows why. Maybe he saw that Vanny was useless, idk. It was likely a last minute idea, so it makes total sense.
- F-ck the saving system. At 6 AM, it gets turned off and you can't even use the previously known cheat that allowed you to save again. They updated that, but none of the bugs, good job. So, after you get to 6 AM, all you have is a total of 1 existing saving point, in a huge, buggy map that can softlock you at any point.

[This may contain light spoilers about gameplay mechanics, but will not discuss the lore of the game, except for when I discuss 6AM mode, at the bottom of the cons list.]

[PROS IN COMMENTS!- Yes, I do enjoy a lot about this game!)

[h1]Cons:[/h1] 

>[b]UNFINISHED[/b]

[b]---->[/b]  I paid $40 for this game, and it isn't finished. It's clear that this game had not even been quality-tested before its release. 
[b]---->[/b] The game is 80GB but for no reason. Arbitrary, meaningless assets are fully-detailed (textures on walls/floors/random junk to fill up a room, etc.). Assets that are actually important gameplay-wise are not detailed enough (s.t.a.f.f. robots moving at a lower frame rate than everything else.) Often, I go into the atrium and stare into a black void for a couple seconds before the room renders in. 
[b]---->[/b] It is very laggy and buggy. Most noticeably in spaces with too many assets (a crowded room, or a battle with several animatronics active.) This not only makes for an unenjoyable experience,  but feels frustrating and unfair when you die to an animatronic due to lagging. (I played on the lowest visual setting, on a gaming computer.)



>[b]QUALITY-OF-LIFE[/b]
[b]---->[/b] This game does not properly use autosaves. There are a plethora of manual save stations throughout the game, but some would be unnecessary if there were appropriate autosaves. It's expected that, when you get to an important part in the game, that it would autosave. (Say, before a boss fight. But The game relies on the player manually saving beforehand.) This game does have some autosaves, but they are random and, in my opinion, misused. 
[b]---->[/b] On a related note, autosaves should be able to start the player off [i]after[/i] a line of unskippable dialogue or cutscene. (i.e. the Lost and Found office, Monty Fight, 6AM reload). These are areas where players might die often (I did), and having to sit through the dialogue every time is- frankly- annoying. 
[b]---->[/b] Freddy's battery (without upgrades) is unreliably short. He might be on 3 bars for 30sec, and then 2 bars for half a second before immediately dropping to 1. 
[b]---->[/b]This game should be linear, not choose-your-own. If you go to Monty Golf before Fazer Blast (how I played) the game is basically on hard mode. There's no reason for this. The game is already free-roam, which is fun. Making it non-linear does nothing but make it confusing, and harder than it needs to be.

>[b]MISSIONS[/b]
[b]---->[/b] These need to be more reliable. The player [i]cannot[/i] rely on [u]key information[/u] about [u]major events[/u] given [i]solely[/i] by Freddy one time, and not repeated or reiterated elsewhere. No chat log, anything. (i.e, getting into Roxy Raceway by climbing stacked boxes). I have seen so many people confused on where to go, and how to get to places, because the information they needed came from Freddy and no where else.
[b]---->[/b] The Missions log is not intuitive, and very confusing. They need to be more-detailed, and actually lead the player where they need to go.


>[b]KEY ITEMS[/b]
[b]---->[/b] These need to be more noticeable. And the player needs to be led to them. It is so, so easy to overlook key items in this game. (i.e. Dance Pass in Roxy Raceway.) This causes backtracking and frustration.
[b]---->[/b] Important key items should not be in gift boxes; they need to be in something completely unique to them. Otherwise, it is easy to overlook them as some random collectible (that not everyone cares about)- and that's if you even find them in the first place.


>[b]INVENTORY[/b]
[b]---->[/b] Personally, I think the inventory should be a tab on the TAB menu screen, not the ESC menu screen. The ESC menu screen is expected to be non-in-game options (Settings, Audio, Visual, Control, Exit Game, etc.) The TAB menu is for in-game items, so the inventory should be there.
[b]---->[/b] Inventory items need descriptions. It is very confusing to pick up something labeled 'Freddy Upgrade,' and have no idea what it does.This could easily be solved by a description for each item on the Inventory screen. Both key items and lore items. Lore item descriptions would be a lot of fun and add more flavor to the game, and key item descriptions are just kinda necessary. 

>[b]MAP[/b]
[b]---->[/b]The map is not useful. Nothing is labeled, And the way it is laid out is not intuitive. Even if areas were only labeled after you visited them, that would be okay. They aren't labeled at all, and it is confusing.
[b]---->[/b]Freddy will say "I've marked it on your map," but he hasn't. The only things ever marked on your map are the recharge stations (not all of them, even), and Freddy's location (which, to be honest, doesn't even matter because he can teleport to your location so long as you're in an area that can summon him. The map key has icons that literally are never, ever used. 

>[b]MAZERCISE[/b]
[b]---->[/b]Mazercise is very difficult and very confusing. I'll run out of characters if I talk about all of its flaws. It's broken.


>[b]6AM MODE[/b]
[b]---->[/b] Overly punishing. It isn't challenging, it's just unfair and frustrating. Especially when the game has so many rando-deaths. ([spoiler]Freddy killing you if you mess up in Parts and Service, seemingly absolutely random Endoskeletons in Bonnie Bowling[/spoiler]) At this point, there is still a(at least) 1 major boss battle, and multiple areas that still need to be explored by the player. It is not fun to explore and make progress when you know a single death takes it all away.
[b]---->[/b] This is a free-roam, lore-based game. If you are going to have collectibles, people are going to want to collect all of them! Especially the Retro disks, which are only available late-game. Again, it is not fun to go around collecting everything, and then lose it when you die.
[b]---->[/b] I can only imagine there is a final boss fight with [spoiler]Vanny[/spoiler], and I cannot imagine going through everything just to die there, and have to restart, finish the last boss, and get to that point all over again. I have gotten as far as all of the upgrades, only to die to really inconsequential things, and it's just frustrating, and does not incite the player to want to keep trying.
[b]---->[/b] if you want to up the difficulty, consider only having a few save stations active, instead of doing away with every single one. The general consensus, I've noticed, about 6AM mode is that it's unfulfilling, frustrating, and unfair. The game is inherently punishing the players that care enough to [i]want[/i] to stay and figure out all the lore. (myself included.) 
[b]---->[/b] It bears repeating that I paid $40 for this game, and the "True Ending" is kept behind a difficulty wall. That is not only unfair, but insulting.

[hr][/hr]

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

I would not be so harsh if this wasn't FNAF. At the end of the day, despite whether the studio has made a game like this before or not, I don't care. FNAF is a million-dollar IP, and the makers of this game [i]knew[/i] it would sell. I'm not going to go light on a studio that released an unfinished game and lined their pockets with it. The marketing for this game really sold it as this polished, put-together experience when it wasn't, and that's grossly irresponsible. I am upset to have paid $40 for a game worth a lot less in its current state. And the difficulty of 6AM mode is like a slap-in-the-face. You can't even enjoy the entire experience, and the base game has no replayability. This game reeks of 'release it now, patch it later,' which is such a disgusting sales model that I have never and will never respect.

Without or prior to the RUIN DLC:
This is a game full of frustrating promise. The first half of the game is a thrilling Alien: Isolation-lite but wrapped in the skin of Fnaf. They laser-focused it so I can actually recommend it. The full free-roam pizzaplex has been cut down to a linear narrative, but this tighter focus allows for a sensation of constantly being hunted. It gives you puzzles that fit within the natural gameplay flow instead of obstructing it with a traffic jam. A savvy player may figure out in what ways the game actually presents the main dangers and can easily avoid it, but then more pressure is added to keep you on your toes.
This isn't the base game Security Breach, but it has the atmosphere and dread that Security Breach wishes it has. If you must play Security Breach, Ruin is essential. And most attractively of all, the DLC is *free*.

To start things off I thoroughly enjoyed this game. But with saying that its definitely not my favorite fnaf game. Far from it actually. While I enjoyed this game I honestly don't know if I can say that its a good game. I'd like to break this down by key elements to a fnaf game so that people can jump to whatever section they care most about. Ill also add a tl;dr at the end of every section so you can get the gist. We can start with...

Game play
Fnaf has had a rather stagnant game play formula since the beginning. Core fnaf game play was basically look and hear your surroundings, react to avoid dying, survive til 6 am. This style was the norm until fnaf 4. Security Breach however heavily shakes up the formula. The game play is more akin to a modern indie survival horror game or hide and seek type of style with some free roaming exploration. You might be thinking, "Oh this guy doesn't like the game cuz its different from old fnaf." As a counterpoint however I argue that Sister Location and Pizzeria Sim heavily shook up the formula and those continue to be my favorite fnaf games to this day. I think the difference is execution. Sister Location took classic fnaf elements and combined them with a more freestyle task based system allowing for more creativity and inovation without destroying the core fnaf principals. Pizzaria simuatior added a resteraunt management system but stayed true to its vent crawling, jumpscare filled, roots. This game is Scott Cawthon and steelwool's first delve into a different type of gameplay and it really shows. The two elements of breath of the wild type exploration and indie horror hide and seek really clash. The game does not hold your hand at all with the occasional vague guest like "Destroy Chica" and forces you to figure out how and where you have to go too destroy chica. This wouldn't be an issue in an open world exploration game where you have all the time in the world to explore but of course this isnt that type of game and as such struggles because of it. In this game you have Freddy your partner and getaway vehicle. He's basically the answer to being able to explore somewhere without having to hide and fear getting killed. The only caveat is that he has VERY limited battery life. This insanely short battery life with no way to recharge except at very sparse recharge stations, causes him to not really fulfill his purpose all too well and makes it very taxing to want to explore as you have to worry about his charge the whole time and if you end up getting stuck with a dead Freddy in a dangerous area, you better hope you saved because there's no way you'll be getting back safely. Basically this game tries to be a indie survival horror which ends up being hurt by its big maps and open world meaning the animatronics have to teleport all the time to even be a danger to you, causing many issues with dying when you shouldn't have and the game being easily breakable. At the same time it tries to be an exploration game but the overabundance of teleporting bots makes it a huge slog to travel especially when your destination might not even be where you need to go. This brings me to another issue which is the linearity of this supposedly open world game. This game basically boils down to completing a linear set of objectives with 2 branching paths along the way that quickly reconnect after a short section. This makes the exploration of the game pointless and just leaves you wondering where to go most of the time. Despite the massive over world of this game there really is only 1 thing at a time you need to do maybe 2 at those branching sections i mentioned earlier. This makes the over world feel extremely empty especially because there isn't much incentive to explore other than items that you can barely call collectibles as collecting them does nothing. This mixed with the fact the game struggles to tell you where to go makes for a game play experience akin to a blind dog walking around an empty room bumping his body into every nook and cranny trying to make it to find his destination until he eventually finds his owner.
Tl;dr: Mix of survival horror and open world exploration gameplay makes for a very empty over world which is frustratingly hard to navigate despite the story being very linear.

Glitches/unfinished game
Yes this does need to be its own section and no i wish it didn't. Im just going to be blunt about this. This game feels unfinished. Somehow despite the countess delays this game still feels like an early alpha release of an indie horror game. I have personally experienced so many glitches im surprised this game want developed by sega. Ill be marking any glitches I personally encountered with a + so you can see what I mean. This game is so bad with glitches and I again attribute that to the clashing game play types. The linearity of this open world game means entering somewhere you aren't supposed to be can soft lock you+, trigger a cut scene that ends up resetting your game state to a much earlier part of the game+, or get you stuck somewhere that forces you to+. I will now name even more glitches that happened to me during my play through so you can get the idea. Got jump scared but not killed and instead teleported to the inside of a wall+, got killed by an animatronic that fell through the roof/appeared from out of the floor+, cheesed the true endings final boss by getting an animatronic stuck in a bed+, got jump scared while in Freddy somehow+, got jump scared while in Freddy again but this time it teleported us into a door and I had to wait for Freddy to run out of battery to finally die and escape+, and finally my personal favorite... the countless times when an animatronic teleported inside of me and instantly killed me+++++++. This is still only some of the glitches I encountered but along with these glitches, the animatronics just... aren't programmed well. Sometimes an animatronic will sense you from the floor above you and glitch through the floor to curb stomp you while sometimes you just stand in front of one without it noticing you. Overall this game just does not feel complete whether its the countless glitches or the horrible ui. Speaking of the ui oh my god it sucks so bad. First of all the starting menu is missing so much that normally comes with a fnaf game like some sort of ending tracker or maybe an extras section. This game literally only has options, start, and quit. The in game menu is much worse. It look like a pause menu for an old fnaf game with just the options and quit. This seems fine until you realize this is an exploration game. All of those items and upgrades you collect get send to a items option which just shows you the items without any options to do stuff with them or see what they are or anything you'd expect. Another bad ui option is the map. Wow its bad. Unless im stupid and missed something you can't zoom in to see the very small map and the icons it says you'll be able to use to navigate just aren't there. Also there are no indications of the area you're in on the map making it very hard to find a named location like the "Mazersize" place. All in all the game feels like an early alpha build made by an indie studio to promote their kick starter and then never actually finish the game.
Tl;dr: Game has countless glitches and an unpolished ui making is seems more like an early alpha release then a 40 dollar game.

Story
Last but not least the story. I have less to say about this one because a good story vs a bad story is very subjective but ill try my best. This is the first fnaf game with a speaking protagonist which is a cool new twist. Nothing much comes of this thought as it's just used to talk to Freddy, your companion throughout the game.  I dont have many more character to write with so ill finish this off by saying the story is lacking with very little actual story even in the 6 or so endings the game has to unlock especially compared to sister locations story.

[u][b]Pros:[/b][/u]
- The atmosphere can be suitably light-hearted or eerily dark when needed.
- The Pizzaplex is so damn cool to look at and is just really visually appealing. There are also tons of easter eggs and references scattered across the attractions that FNaF fans will be pleased to see. 
- The animatronics, for better or for worse, all have distinct and memorable personalities. It's a plus to me however, as I feel that their personalities mesh well with the overall tone of the game.
- The endo section at 3AM is an actual nightmare to go through on a blind playthrough (in a good way).
- The music, and the sound design in general, slaps.
- It's very possible and valid to play this game with stealth, i.e. crouching behind objects, making distractions, utilising hiding spots and watching the cameras to plan your next move, which really amps up the tension and overall mood of the game in a way that I suspect was the intended method of playing.
- The free Ruin DLC, which adds a whole new campaign with a new protagonist following the events of the base game, does an incredible job of improving on many negative aspects of the base game, most of which are covered in the cons section of this review.


[u][b]Cons:[/b][/u]
- The game has a recurring habit of telling you to go somewhere in the Pizzaplex, only to then say that you're missing an item of importance and instructs you to go to some other location a mile away then come back with said important item.
- Couple instances of poorly guided progression, i.e. no clear indication of where to go next, or the game gives you a hint on what to do only once, and never repeats it ever again.
- The provided map of the Pizzaplex is poorly designed, which is a shame, considering the point above.
- The overabundance of STAFF bots are an absolute pain in the butt to deal with at times.
- Post-6AM spawns the only usable save station in the atrium balcony. All other save stations are disabled. This is both a pro and a con in my opinion, since it really adds to the tension of getting through the final animatronic decommission without dying, but can also lead to loss of both time and effort either through loss of progress by dying before saving, or having to trudge over to the atrium every time you want to save your progress.
- The game's story might make some FNaF 1~6 lore enthusiasts weep.
- This game takes up a rather unreasonable >80GB of your storage. 
- You need a somewhat decent device to comfortably play this game. Not an absolute high-end build of course, but at least a mid-tier is recommended, while a low-end will most definitely struggle. I recommend checking benchmarks to gauge the expected performance before purchasing.


[u][i]Overall:[/i][/u]
FNaF SB is definitely worth a try in my opinion. While it's far from the best game ever, and also has some untapped potential here and there, provided that you're able to run the game, and have the storage and money to spare, this game is a fun way to pass the time, and is also rather decently replayable. The infamous game-breaking bugs and glitches are also mostly fixed at the time this was written, making now a better time than ever to try the game out. A solid 7/10, though I also recommend buying this game when it's on sale.

Do not buy this game unless you own a more above average system. The optimization is laughable and the gameplay is decent but overall subpar. Incredibly frequent lag spikes, and ray tracing lags even an overclocked 2080ti on my end. The AI is incredibly janky and super unpredictable, and the map is just too big in some cases. Objectives will point you in a direction where you don't know where to look. Imagine using a GPS, and it tells you where you need to go but doesn't show you the route, that is completing objectives in this game. I am requesting a refund until a massive patch comes out which addresses all of the performance issues and gameplay issues. I am honestly disappointed.

So what are my thoughts on security breach? Its hard to say, there's lots of pro's and cons, and I'd like to go into detail with them quickly before I give my final review. Due to how new this game is, I will be keeping it all spoiler free, so dont worry.

Pro's:

1.) The Graphics are amazing as long as you have the system for it
2.) The Animations are amazing, especially in cutscenes where they're intended to be seen in the forefront
3.) As long as you have a decent computer, the game runs rather smoothly, giving you 60+ FPS on High graphics
4.) The environment is ablsolutely beautiful, and well designed, props for that, Steel Wool

Con's:

1.) Almost every mission is just a fetch quest, so if you love running and hiding while looking for the single item you need to progress, then you're in luck
2.) The animatronics have mastered the art of teleportation, this is most prevelant in Chica
3.) The loading zones are very glitchy. if you get unlucky, you'll fall through the floor and softlock
4.) The AI's of the animatronics are very basic, hell, in some sections of the game, the animatronics bug out and get stuck in a loop of the same animations and same locations, no matter where you, or anyone else is
5.) At the beginning of the game, you are told that if Freddy's battery dies, he in unavaliable until the next hour, but he is needed to progress in many parts of the game, so they had the genius idea of just killing you and sending you to your last save
6.) There are no true boss battles like they promised, all of them are just: run, collect things, press buttons, lure the animatronics, get out. They really should've fully fleshed those parts out
7.) Many assets from the game are stock ue4 meshes, no real time put into making them, almost as if they kept the placeholder assets.
8.) I get that human models are hard to make, but they really should've outsourced to someone who can make base models that they could add to. the horrendous looking human models in the amazing looking environment feel very off, and take away from the visual beauty of the game.

Overall, this game is okay. No more, no less. Some aspects are good, some are meh, and the rest are just... bad. I wish they had fully fleshed out the game before they released it. there are way to many fetch quests, way too much backtracking, and most importantly, not enough Vanny. This game is on par with FFPS, and that isn't saying much. I feel a $20 price tag wouldve fit better with this game. Overall, I give this game a 6.5/10

Want to start out by saying that I didn't play any FNAF games after the first one, just watched it from gameplay videos and livestreams but I'm really invested in the storyline of FNAF.

FNAF Security Breach was a great experience for me. Despite having some issues with bugs, overall the game was enjoyable and it was a different (but good) experience. FNAF taking a turn and making a 3D game with an Entertainment Mall as the map was a great idea (I know there is FNAF Help Wanted but it was for VR). The mall was well designed and it looked very pleasing. The details were really good and the shops and all the things that are in the mall was designed really great, it felt like an authentic Entertainment Mall. Exploring it was really great with all the paths you can take.

The whole point of playing a child protagonist hiding, running away and try to escape from Murderer Animatronics in 3D was overall a nerving experience. I’ll admit that the Jumpscares are not as scary as the other FNAF games, mostly due to the game being 3D so you can understand if an Animatronic was chasing you or not, unlike the other games where the jumpscares happened in an instant making them more scary/startling. Still the whole chasing and playing the game stealthy trying not to get caught was great.

The gameplay loop was well designed, the movement system felt great. The 6 nights return from the original games and in this game, after passing a certain night *minor spoiler*[spoiler]you start hunting down the Animatronics that were hunting you and they turn into a Little Boss fight type of thing. After beating them, you use the parts you gather to upgrade Freddy’s utility. By beating them, they actually don’t disappear fully but rather they turn into withered versions of themselves which is really creepy. [/spoiler] At the 6th night, you ultimately try to escape the mall. There are different endings too and one of them is especially really nice :) The mission system was great too, you can take diferrent paths for the same mission.

There was a part in a certain mission where *minor spoiler* [spoiler]you try to escape from unused endoskeletons.[/spoiler] This was by far the most scary, nervous and thrilling part of the game. I loved it.

One of the most discussed topic for this game, Vanny/Vannessa. I honestly was expecting much more from her, like all the others were. I think this was due to Steel Wool trying to deliver the game asap rather then taking their time to polish it because leakers found more things about Vanny in the game. I did not have any expectations going into the game but this part was a little disappointing, still for me, it did not take the fun out of the game.

There are collectibles too, some of them are just for the achievements and some of them are upgrades for you and Freddy.  You can upgrade your stamina, sprinting speed, stealthiness etc with gathering certain collectibles. Thought this was a really neat idea.

They also announced the new free DLC "Ruin" for the game which will come out in 2023. First of all, I’m really glad they will release the DLC free, and second of all, with the poster they released in the announcement it seems like the DLC will be about what happened after a certain ending which seems to be the cannon one. Really looking forward to playing it!

So, I would recommend getting the game if you want to experience a new type of FNAF game that looks really good. Despite it having bugs overall the game is fun, enjoyable and thrilling.

[h1]I want to love this game, but...[/h1]
My friends and I were pretty excited to play this game, and it being playable on steam was icing on the cake.  Now I'm able to stream it to them since its a bit of a pricey game with some respectable PC requirements.  However, while this game does look very good on say, edited videos and clips on YT, watching it live or playing it will show the excess amount of cracks that keeps this game at either best case frustrating to worst case Sonic Boom: RoL levels of unplayable.  
I will say that the game theoretically has a good experience, a lot of tense and thrilling moments, decent challenges, good art direction and sound design, and that good ol' Scott Cawthon charm.  I feel most of the issues comes down to execution, not like weird design choices or bad pacing, I mean how the game plays on an engine level.  Higher graphics and Raytracing absolutely destroys the game by making it super choppy when looking around.  I was forced to play on the lowest settings on my RTX 3070, and this is all apparent in the first MINUTE of gameplay (hell it was showing up in the title screen).  Just screen tearing and massive frame drops that make the game lag and disorients the player (I'm rarely a stickler for things like technical graphics and stuff like that.).  
The game is poorly optimized and doesn't really feel finished.  A lot of areas load in front of you, and have questionable lighting choices even for a horror game.  There are many cutscenes that just look way too dark and make it difficult to see, when direction wise there doesn't seem to be an emphasis on giving a mystery to a character.  If you can look past the visual bugs, the game is filled to the brim with game breaking glitches and plenty of minor ones that can easily get you a game over if you're not ready for it.  You can easily set off events that weren't supposed to happen and softlock the game or force a death.  These issues are impossible to ignore and I've even thought to myself multiple times "Were there playtesters?  Why didn't anyone listen?  There's no way they would let this launch at this state?  There are a lot of rookie mistakes in here."  
I haven't even talked about the base game, how would it play if it were completely bug free?  Well, there's a lot of highs and lows.  The tense moments feel great and bring back the similar feeling of "Panic and Fear while Puzzling" the series has always done well.  But the game does leave the player with plenty of "bad confusion" or "bad conveyance."  The first few FNaF games did give the player confusion with vague advice from the phone guy, but that added to the experience.  This game clearly tells you the mechanics which leaves the player to just complete the challenge, which is nice...  Until you're wandering the colossal building for 10 minutes because they want you to find a pin in a haystack, or when you think you've picked up an enemy's pattern/quirk then they teleport through a wall or do something that doesn't feel right game design wise.  I know I'm being pretty vague, but its a subtle yet common problem.  These lows probably wouldn't feel that bad if the game wasn't so buggy, but I just wanted to put it out there.  
This game has so much potential to be a really good experience, but I can't recommend a 40 dollar unfinished game that takes like 20+ hours to 100% .  Either wait for it to go on sale, or just watch a YTuber play it.

Before all the die-hard Five Nights and Freddy's fans start dog-piling me for giving this game a negative review, let me explain myself.

I want to like this game, and I want to give it a positive review - but I also want to be able to play the game in the first place, because the optimization for this game is actually worse than the optimization for the Halo Infinite Multiplayer Beta when that launched.

Sure, there's been a couple moments here-and-there at the start where I was able to move around with relatively no lag, but - in it's current state - between the horrific load times and bouts of lag that took upwards of 30 seconds to cull an area or load a couple textures, I honestly can't justify this game taking up 80 GB of space on my hard-drive.

I've also seen a lot of discussions posts about just how buggy this game is as well, which is honestly a shame. I get that - at the time of writing this - the game basically just came out, but for all the time it's spent being in development and how many times it's been delayed, I'm honestly disappointed.

However, I'm staying optimistic simply for the fact that this is a Five Nights at Freddy's game, and even though Scott has retired, there's no doubt in my mind that these issues will be resolved one day - the guy always listens to his fans.

But, as far as the game currently goes - I don't have the space to just let it sit here and collect virtual dust... So, in short; buy at your own risk, there have been people like me with some decent gaming PC's that are having these issues, and there are also people with higher-end gaming PC's that are also having these issues.

This game is like a car crash. It's horrific and broken, but I can't stop looking at it.

I cannot support developers releasing a game with so many bugs, even developers that have great concepts. It's a 5/5 for story and design, but a 2/5 on execution.

The story, concept, sound design, and art are all great. However, there are SO MANY quality of life issues in this game.

Story triggers can be re-triggered multiple times, even out of order (it often takes saving, quitting, and reloading, but it works).

Turning sprint toggle OFF still internally treats it like a toggle. As in, it ONLY checks the moment you press shift if you can run. If you press shift when you cannot run due to something, and then move forward, you won't be running anyways. Kind of important when running from bots.

Turning save points off at various points in the story is UTTER GARBAGE. My mouse double-bounces sometimes, and having to do the stupid Simon Says puzzles EVERY TIME I load my save is just ridiculous garbage.

Trigger spaces for many hide spots or other triggers do not extend up to the object itself, so you can run PAST the trigger space that lets you use the item simply by running towards it too far. They also don't feel wide/big enough in many cases.

The camera map shows cameras that have activity on them with a "!" in the view. The problem is, once this symbol goes away, it resets it to a PLAIN camera tile. This frequently ends up removing the "selected" camera graphic, which makes it very obnoxious in areas with many cameras to know which one you're viewing.

There are TONS of bugs around the sneak notifier. It's red or yellow half the time when there's not even a robot in the area to chase me!

There are quite a few areas where you can get trapped or soft-locked just by exploring around to areas you maybe shouldn't. Sure, it happens in many games, but it's A LOT in this one, and there are semi-hidden collectibles encouraging exploration.

The robots are painfully stupid and are only present during a shockingly few set of segments/areas. It feels like for half the game, I'm just running around with only security guards who don't even spawn a robot 90% of the time to chase me if I'm spotted. When they DO spawn, it's only a single bot even if I'm in a HUGE area, making them literally zero threat. That's before you get items to help escape them.

Many of the story points and tasks have poorly designed order of operations and 'hints' as to where to go or what to do. Most notably, in the pizza kitchen with Chica if you go there after clearing the arcade. You can open all doors and explore to your heart's content, which means you can easily leave without completing the tasks there.

There are tons of other spots like that where the mission wants you to do something, or the flavor text says something, yet if you do exactly what it says, either nothing happens or you die. Like when Vanessa leaves something for you on the stage towards the end. Don't go to the stage, because the Moon's going to kill you anyways!!

The story is absolutely broken as far as progress and getting all of the items. If you choose to get the camera, you CANNOT destroy Chica (nothing happens when you place the goo to attract her, no button appears, nothing), which means you cannot open some gates, since some areas are gated by her item.

You CANNOT reenter the daycare to collect items you've missed. At all. Ever. Unless there's a hidden passage where the sun doesn't kick you out of, but that'd make little sense.

If you choose the camera (golf), you CANNOT get the Vanny ending without doing the ENTIRE PHAZER BLASTER AREA without saves, and THEN Vanny without a save after the blaster area. That's assuming it even lets me choose Vanny when going to leave for a second time AFTER doing the blaster area.

There are tons of other little bugs, like the Moon/Sun's sound node staying behind when he despawns. I've had robots run up to me, run half of the capture animation, and set me down ... just to fully capture me when I move next. I've sat in a bin with a robot staring at me until I get out just to capture me. I've had robots spawn in two feet away REPEATEDLY as I run away just for them to catch me when I stagger in to them for not realizing they're two feet away all of the sudden for the fifth time in a row.

The game soft-locks if you use the upgrade PC while inside Freddy. Bad play testing. I've also fallen through the floor exiting Freddy.

I've hit every single button on my keyboard and mouse, and literally nothing works for 'use' in Princess Quest I. I had to quit and reload and it suddenly worked. What the actual hell?

The game is 80GB, and the asset streaming is poorly optimized. There are several areas, mostly in the lower areas of the stage and in the back hallways where Freddy initially helps you get towards the front, where the game is CONSTANTLY either loading assets, or it's freaking out about placing all the loaded security bots/etc. I have 11GB of gfx RAM. I have 32 GB of system RAM. Why is the game never using more than 3-5GB, yet having such load issues? It's trying to load tons of stupid other things when you're running around LOCKED areas, which makes for horrible, jittery frames.

Really, there aren't THAT many individual issues poisoning this game outside of a couple REALLY POOR design decisions, a lack of optimization, and a handful of INCREDIBLY obnoxious bugs and wrinkles in the story/mission cues. It'd take a competent dev team maybe one or two more months to polish this up. Why the hell was it released in this buggy form?? To get here for the holiday season?

Gee thanks. I love seeing lovely indie devs turn in to trashy, bug-ridden, premature releasing "AAA" devs... I love the concept of this game, but FIX IT, please. I will not explore 1/3rd of the entire freaking game with saves disabled.
